10	
11	- Create a new Flow project with `uip maestro flow init`

20	## Node ownership — who authors the node
21	
22	Every node in a `.flow` file has exactly one author. The validator enforces this.
23	
24	**User-owned nodes (Edit / Write directly):**
25	
26	| Category | Node types |
27	| --- | --- |
28	| Triggers | `core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled` |
29	| Control flow | `core.logic.decision`, `core.logic.switch`, `core.logic.loop`, `core.logic.merge`, `core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`, `core.subflow` |
30	| Logic | `core.action.script`, `core.action.transform`, `core.logic.delay`, `core.logic.mock` |
31	| Human-in-the-loop | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (inline form), `uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app` (app-based) |
32	| Patterns | `uipath.pattern.batch-transform`, `uipath.pattern.deep-rag` |
33	| Agents | `uipath.agent.autonomous` (inline; after `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`) |
34	| Resource nodes | `uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.agent.*`, `uipath.core.flow.*`, `uipath.core.agentic-process.*`, `uipath.core.api-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.human-task.*` |
35	| Queue | `core.action.queue.create`, `core.action.queue.create-and-wait` |
36	
37	**CLI-owned nodes (`uip maestro flow node add` + `uip maestro flow node configure`):**
38	
39	| Category | Node types | Why |
40	| --- | --- | --- |
41	| Connector activities | `uipath.connector.<key>.<op>` | `inputs.detail` is a `=jsonString:essentialConfiguration` envelope. Validate rejects hand-authored shapes. |
42	| Connector triggers | `uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>` | Same envelope + product-managed `bindings_v2.json` derivation. |
43	| Wait for events (mid-flow) | `uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>` | Same envelope and event metadata as a trigger, but placed mid-flow (has an `input` port) instead of as the start node. See [connector-trigger/impl.md — Wait for events](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md#wait-for-events-uipathconnectoreventkeyevent). |
44	| Managed HTTP | `core.action.http.v2` | Same envelope. |
45	
46	For CLI-owned nodes:
47	
48	- Use `uip maestro flow node add` to insert the node and copy the definition into `definitions[]`.
49	- Use `uip maestro flow node configure --detail '{...}'` to populate `inputs.detail` and `bindings[]`.
50	- Subsequent edits to `inputs.detail` are also CLI-only — re-run `node configure` (it's a full rebuild; see [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md)).
51	- You may still `Edit` the node's `display.label`, edges, layout, and outputs — those are not part of the envelope.
52	
53	If you find yourself hand-writing `inputs.detail`, a `=jsonString:` blob, or `bindings[]` entries for a connector node — stop. Use the CLI.
54	
55	## Critical rules
56	
57	1. **Always validate node types against the registry before building.** Use `registry search`/`list` for discovery and `registry get` for detailed metadata and definitions.
58	2. **ALWAYS follow the relevant plugin in [plugins/](references/plugins/) for every node type.** Each plugin has a `planning.md` (when to use, selection heuristics, ports) and `impl.md` (registry validation, JSON structure, CLI commands, configuration, debug). For connector nodes, the [connector](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) plugin covers connection binding, enriched metadata, and field resolution — required before building. Without this, node configuration will be wrong — errors that `flow validate` does not catch.
59	3. **Read the relevant Integration Service reference doc before any `uip is ...` call.** Two non-overlapping contracts:
60	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md) before any `uip is connections ...` call.** Applies to every connector activity, connector trigger, and managed HTTP node in connected mode. Single source of truth for command syntax, selection (including the personal-workspace auto-select rule), folder scoping, BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, and ping verification. **If no healthy connection exists after following its recovery flow, STOP** and surface it in **Open Questions** during planning.
61	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — resources.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) before any `uip is resources run ...` call.** Applies to every reference-field lookup (Slack user IDs, Jira project keys, Outlook folder IDs, etc.). Single source of truth for the `Data.Pagination.HasMore` / `NextPageToken` contract and the `--query "nextPage=<token>"` loop. **Complete the pagination loop before reporting not-found** — do NOT abandon mid-loop to try alternative endpoints, `where=` filters the connector may not support, or asking the user. Plugin files cover node-specific configuration that follows connection binding: [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), [http/impl-connector.md](references/plugins/http/impl-connector.md).
62	4. **Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` only** — other generated files (`bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`, `operate.json`, `package-descriptor.json`) are managed by the CLI and may be overwritten. To declare flow inputs/outputs, add variables in the `.flow` file (see [shared/file-format.md](../shared/file-format.md)).
63	5. **`targetPort` is required on every edge** — `validate` rejects edges without it.
64	6. **Every node type needs a `definitions` entry** — copy from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type>` output. Never hand-write definitions. The definition is the sole source for BPMN type (`model.type`), serviceType, event definitions, and binding/context templates — none of that belongs on the instance.
65	7. **Script nodes must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar.
66	8. **Validate once at the end** — run `uip maestro flow validate` only after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual node add or edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
67	9. **Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file** — there are no CLI commands for variable management. Use `Edit` to add/remove/update entries in the `variables` section of the `.flow` file. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
68	10. **Every `out` variable must be mapped on every reachable End node** — missing output mappings cause runtime errors. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
69	11. **`=js:` prefix is REQUIRED on every `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` reference in a value field** — not on condition expressions (decision, switch, HTTP branch), which are auto-evaluated as JS. Without it, the BPMN runtime sees a literal string and `flow validate` fails with MST-9107. See [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the canonical rule and per-node-type field reference, and [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the expression system.
70	12. **Always run `flow format` after edits** — `uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow` is the canonical layout step. Format arranges nodes horizontally, sets each node's `size` by its canvas shape (inline agents → 288×96, containers → 560×320, everything else → 96×96), and recurses into subflows (`subflows[<id>].layout`). Skipping format is the most common cause of misshapen nodes in Studio Web.
71	13. **Don't hand-write `layout.nodes` or `subflows[<id>].layout`** — these are owned by `flow format`. When authoring nodes, any placeholder `position` is fine (e.g. `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); format rewrites it on save. Sticky notes (`type: "stickyNote"`) are the one exception — format preserves their custom size and position. See [shared/file-format.md — Layout](../shared/file-format.md#layout).
72	14. **Every data-producing node MUST have a matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — this is what makes `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolve.** The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput>` declarations the runtime needs. The instance `outputs` block is **only** consumed by BPMN serialization on end-style nodes (to map workflow-level `out` variables); for action / trigger nodes it is documentation, not behavior. Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). **Always run `uip maestro flow format` after structural edits — it regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`** (matching what `uip maestro flow node add` and the canvas save path do), so this becomes self-healing as long as you `format`. See [shared/file-format.md — Node outputs](../shared/file-format.md#node-outputs).
73	15. **Node instances have no `model` block** — BPMN type, serviceType, version, event definitions, and binding/context templates live in the node's **definition** (in the top-level `definitions[]` array, copied verbatim from `registry get`). The runtime hydrates these from the definition at serialization time. Instance-specific identity fields live under `inputs`: `entryPointId`, `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers), `color`/`content` (sticky notes), and `source` (every inline-agent-related node — both `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node use `inputs.source = <UUID>`; their definitions declare `model.source: true` and flow-core hoists onto the instance).

112	## Anti-patterns
113	
114	- **Prefer running `uip maestro flow init` from inside the solution you named** — run outside one it auto-scaffolds `<Project>Solution/`, but the auto name won't match your chosen solution name. Never pass `--skip-solution-registration` for a project you intend to upload (it leaves a bare single-nested layout). See [SKILL.md rule #6](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) for the required double-nested `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` layout and the self-check.
115	- **Never guess node schemas** — use `registry get` for all node types. Guessed port names or input fields cause silent wiring failures.
116	- **Never skip capability discovery for connector nodes** — run `registry search` to confirm the connector exists and what operations it supports before building. See [connector/planning.md](references/plugins/connector/planning.md). Skipping this is the #1 cause of designing around a connector that doesn't exist or an operation it doesn't support.
117	- **Never replace a registered connector operation with `core.logic.mock` because configuration cannot run** — if `registry search` / `registry get` finds `uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<operation>`, add that real connector node via `uip maestro flow node add`. Missing live connections, missing tenant access, or prompts that ask you to only plan `--detail` mean: run `node add`, write the planned `--detail` payload to a sidecar file (e.g. `<nodeId>.detail.json`), and surface "configure pending" as an Open Question. **Do not leave a partial `inputs.detail` on the node** — the validator rejects hand-authored envelopes, and the node will not pass `flow validate` until `node configure` is run. Studio Web and reviewers need the real connector key in the `.flow`; the agent must report this explicitly rather than letting the user discover it via a later validation failure. See [§ Node ownership](#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) and [connector/impl.md — No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration](references/plugins/connector/impl.md#no-live-tenant--planned-configuration).
118	- **Never edit `content/*.bpmn`** — it is auto-generated from the `.flow` file and will be overwritten.
119	- **Never use `core.logic.mock` when the resource is in the same solution** — use `--local` discovery instead. Mock placeholders are only for resources that are not in the current solution and not yet published.
120	- **Never hand-write `definitions` entries** — always copy from registry output. Hand-written definitions have wrong port schemas and cause validation failures.
121	- **Never put any `model` block on node instances** — BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, binding templates, and context templates all live in the node's **definition** (copied verbatim from `registry get` into `definitions[]`). Instances carry only per-instance data: `inputs`, `outputs`, `display`. Identity fields like `entryPointId` / `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers) and `color` / `content` (sticky notes) live under `inputs`. This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source = <UUID>`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance.
122	- **Never author `model.context[]` on resource-node instances** — resource-node instances have no `model` block. For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition (from `registry get`) already carries `model.context[]` with `<bindings.{name}>` placeholders. Your job is to add matching entries to the top-level `bindings[]` array — two entries per resource node (`name` + `folderPath`) with `resourceKey` matching the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`. At BPMN emit, the runtime rewrites `<bindings.{name}>` → `=bindings.{id}` via `(resourceKey, name)` matching. Without the top-level `bindings[]` entries, `uip maestro flow validate` passes but `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder." See the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
123	- **Never put a `ui` block on node instances** — position and size belong in the top-level `layout.nodes` object. Nodes with `"ui": { "position": ... }` use the wrong format and may not render correctly in Studio Web.
124	- **Never skip `flow format` before publish or debug** — without it, hand-written `layout` data renders as misshapen rectangles in Studio Web (the MST-9061 failure mode). See rule #12 above for the format step.
125	- **Never validate after every individual edit** — intermediate flow states (e.g., node added but not yet wired) are expected to be invalid. Run `uip maestro flow validate` once after the full build is complete.
126	- **Never use `console.log` in script nodes** — `console` is not available in the Jint runtime. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
127	- **Never forget output mapping on End nodes** — every `out` variable in `variables.globals` must have a `source` expression in every reachable End node's `outputs`. Missing mappings cause silent runtime failures.
128	- **Never update `in` variables** — only `inout` variables can be modified via `variableUpdates`. Input variables are read-only after flow start.
129	- **Never reference parent-scope `$vars` inside a subflow** — subflows have isolated scope. Pass values explicitly via subflow inputs.

Strip it and pass an array value of the field's `dataType` (e.g. `"fields.labels[*]"` → `"fields.labels": ["a", "b"]`). Supported only when `[*]` is the name suffix; `[*].` (segments after) is not authorable. `flow validate` misses this; runtime rejects the key. 2

7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10	
11	**Plan when:**
12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach
15	
16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))
18	- The flow is a straightforward linear pipeline (trigger → action → action → end)
19	- The user has already described the exact topology they want
20	
21	### Examples
22	
23	**Plan:** "Build a flow that receives a Jira ticket, classifies it with an AI agent, routes urgent tickets to Slack and non-urgent to a queue, and logs everything to a Google Sheet."
24	→ Multiple services, branching logic, connector discovery needed. Plan first.
25	
26	**Don't plan:** "Create a flow that calls an API and sends the result to Slack."
27	→ Linear pipeline, user knows what they want. Build directly, ask questions inline if needed. **"Build directly" skips the plan doc, not the registry search** — you still `registry search` each named service and pick a node type via the Step 3 ladder.
28	
29	**Judgment call:** "Build me a flow that processes invoices."
30	→ Ambiguous requirements. Ask clarifying questions; plan if answers reveal complexity.
31	
32	## Three-turn execution map
33	
34	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
35	
36	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s) **+** optional `uip login status`. **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
39	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
40	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
41	
42	### Batching anti-patterns
43	
44	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
45	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
46	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
47	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
48	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
49	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

53	See [shared/cli-conventions.md](../../shared/cli-conventions.md) for binary resolution, version detection, and the `uip maestro flow` vs `uip flow` command prefix rule. All commands below are written in the `uip maestro flow` form. <!-- uip-check-skip -->

55	This probe is read-only — emit as a parallel `Bash` alongside the Step 2 scaffold chain. It does not need its own turn.

127	
128	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. 133	  "Code": "FlowInit",
134	  "Data": {

186	If the file does not exist at the absolute double-nested path, Step 2 is wrong. Delete the partial scaffold and restart from Step 2a — do not try to patch the layout by hand.

190	## Step 3 — Refresh the registry **[T1 — chained tail of Step 2]**
191	
192	This is already the last segment of the [canonical T1 chain](#canonical-t1-chain--issue-this-as-one-bash-call) above. Standalone:
193	
194	```bash
195	uip maestro flow registry pull                          # refresh local cache (expires after 30 min)
196	```
197	
198	**Parallel `registry get`** — in the same T1 assistant message, emit one separate `Bash` per OOTB node type whose definition you'll inline in T2. **Always fetch `core.control.end`** — `flow init` does not scaffold one (see Step 4):
199	
200	```bash
201	uip maestro flow registry get core.control.end --output json
202	```
203	
204	> **Auth note**: Without `uip login`, registry shows OOTB nodes only. After login, tenant-specific connector and resource nodes are also available. **In-solution sibling projects** are always available via `--local` without login — see below.
205	
206	### Select the node type for each external service (runs even when full planning is skipped)
207	
208	Calling a named external service (Slack, open-meteo, Stripe, any REST API)? **Search first — never guess the node type from the brand name:**
209	
210	```bash
211	uip maestro flow registry search "<service>" --output json --output-filter "[*].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName,Description:Description,AvailableOnTenant:AvailableOnTenant}"
212	```
213	
214	Then pick the first match down this ladder:
215	
216	1. **Curated connector activity** (`uipath.connector.<key>.<op>` in the results) → use it.
217	2. **Connector exists but no activity for what you need** → `core.action.http.v2` (connector mode).
218	3. **No connector at all** → `core.action.http.v2` (manual mode).
219	4. **No API** (desktop app) → [rpa](plugins/rpa/planning.md).
220	
221	Manual HTTP is the **bottom of the ladder** — only the search returning no connector authorizes it. Picking it without searching is the brand-name shortcut forbidden by [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal).
222	
223	**In-solution discovery (no login required):**
224	
225	```bash
226	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json     # discover sibling projects in the same .uipx solution
227	uip maestro flow registry search "<keyword>" --local --output json  # keyword search across in-solution nodes
228	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json  # get full manifest for a local node
229	```
230	
231	Run from inside the flow project directory. Returns the same manifest format as the tenant registry. Use `--local` to wire in-solution resources (RPA, agents, flows, API workflows) without publishing them first. `search --local` omits `AvailableOnTenant` — drop it from `--output-filter` projections.
232	
233	## Step 4 — Build the flow **[T2]**
234	
235	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. Any HTTP / connector / connector-trigger node you `node add`-ed in T1 is already in `nodes[]` and `definitions[]` but has empty `inputs.detail` (filled in T3) and is not wired yet.
236	
237	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
238	
239	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
240	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
241	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
242	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
243	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
244	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
245	
246	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)).
247	
248	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
249	
250	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
251	
252	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
253	
254	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
255	|---|---|---|
256	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
257	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. Empty after `flow init` (`\n  "edges": []`); the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
258	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
259	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in `init`-scaffolded flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
260	
261	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
262	
263	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
264	
265	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
266	
267	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
268	
269	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
270	
271	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).
272	
273	### Node ownership recap
274	
275	> **Before each node, classify it as user-owned or CLI-owned (see [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)). Connector activities, connector triggers, and `core.action.http.v2` are CLI-only — use `uip maestro flow node add` + `uip maestro flow node configure`, never Edit. Hand-writing these will fail `flow validate`.**
276	
277	Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` directly in the project root. The `bindings_v2.json` file is also in the project root for resource bindings.
278	
279	> **Tool selection by ownership.** Use `Edit` for in-place changes to user-owned nodes; `Write` only when ≥70% of nodes change. For CLI-owned nodes (above), use `uip maestro flow node add` + `node configure` — see the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for the full configuration workflow. Inline-agent project scaffolding uses `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`, but inline-agent flow node/wiring edits are direct `.flow` JSON (the agent node itself is user-owned).
280	
281	Read [editing-operations.md](editing-operations.md) for strategy selection and per-operation recipes.
282	
283	> **Self-check before each mutation:** name the tool you're about to use. If the answer isn't `Edit`, `Write`, or `uip maestro flow ...` — STOP and ask the user (per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). `python`, `node`, `jq`, `sed`, `awk`, and shell heredocs are a last resort and require explicit user approval after you've surfaced the trade-offs. See [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder).
284	
285	For each node type, follow the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for node-specific inputs, JSON structure, and configuration. The operations guides cover the mechanics (how to add/remove/wire); the plugins cover the semantics (what inputs and model fields each node type needs).
286	
287	## Step 5 — Validate **[T3 — chain with Step 6, plus any T1 `node configure`]**
288	
289	### Canonical T3 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
290	
291	```bash
292	uip maestro flow node configure "<ProjectName>.flow" "<httpNodeId>" --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>' --output json \
293	  && uip maestro flow validate "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json \
294	  && uip maestro flow format "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json
295	```
296	
297	`<DETAIL_JSON>` is node-type-specific — the schema is owned by each CLI-owned node's plugin, not duplicated here: HTTP → [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md#critical-use-node-configure), connectors → [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), connector triggers → [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md). Tail-append one `node configure` per CLI-owned node added in T1, using the node IDs captured from T1's chained output. Drop the entire `node configure` segment if no CLI-owned nodes exist.
298	
299	> **The plugin `impl.md` is authoritative — follow its full procedure, not just its `--detail` schema, and let it override this turn map.** A plugin may prescribe steps the three-turn collapse does not show — most importantly a **pre-`configure` live fetch** whose output you must read before you can author `--detail` (the value depends on the live response, so it cannot be guessed or copied from a doc example). When `impl.md` defines such a step, run it in its **own turn before T3** and build `--detail` from its result; do not batch it into the chain, skip it, or hand-author the payload. An empty or static base response is expected for these steps and is not a signal the step is unavailable. This is general to every CLI-owned node type — defer to the owning `impl.md` rather than assuming static config.
300	
301	**On validate failure:** one `Edit` turn to fix, then re-chain `validate && format` in one Bash. Do not validate after every individual Edit during T2 — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
302	
303	> **A passing exit code with warnings is NOT done.** `flow validate` returns 0 even when `Data.Warnings` is non-empty — read the warnings, don't just check the exit code. The connector-keyword warning (`node "…" mentions the "<connector>" connector keyword but uses the generic Managed HTTP type core.action.http.v2 with no connection binding`) means the flow took the brand-name shortcut and will run against an undefined endpoint at debug time — resolve it by switching to the connector before reporting the flow complete (see [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) and the anti-pattern list). Treat this class of warning as a build failure for your own definition of "done."
304	
305	### Common error categories
306	
307	- **Missing targetPort** — every edge needs a `targetPort` string
308	- **Missing definition** — every `type:typeVersion` in nodes needs a matching `definitions` entry
309	- **Invalid node/edge references** — `sourceNodeId`/`targetNodeId` must reference existing node `id`s
310	- **Duplicate IDs** — node and edge `id`s must be unique
311	
312	## Step 6 — Format node layout **[T3 — chained tail of Step 5]**
313	
314	This is the last segment of the [canonical T3 chain](#canonical-t3-chain--issue-this-as-one-bash-call) above. After validation passes, format must run before publishing or debugging (see "Always run `flow format` after edits" in [the Author capability index](../CAPABILITY.md)). Format:
315	
316	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) using ELK with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
317	- Sets each non-stickyNote node's `size` by its canvas shape so Studio Web renders it correctly: inline agents (`shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`, containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`, everything else (incl. referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>`) → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }` (skipping this leaves stale dimensions intact and produces misshapen nodes — the MST-9061 failure mode)
318	- Recurses into subflows and rewrites `subflows[<id>].layout`
319	- Backfills missing `position`/`size` entries
320	
321	Standalone (only if not chained from Step 5):
322	
323	```bash
324	uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow --output json
325	```

332	2. **What was built** — summary of nodes added, edges wired, and logic implemented

1	# HTTP Request Node — Implementation
2	
3	This page is the entry point for implementing a managed HTTP node. Pick your auth mode below, then follow the matching walkthrough end-to-end. The "Shared Reference" section is an appendix — the mode walkthroughs already inline what you need to act, and link here only for full rationale and extended examples.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated.
10	
11	## Pick a Mode
12	
13	| Mode | Use when | Walkthrough |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| **Connector** | Target system has an IS connector — auth via an existing IS connection (OAuth/API key) | [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, public/no-auth API, or quick prototyping | [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md) |
17	
18	> **Mode fallback — auto-try, then confirm.** Prefer a curated connector activity first; if none, use connector mode; if connector mode cannot be configured (connector lacks HTTP request support — `HasHttpRequest` false — or no usable IS connection), fall through to manual mode automatically. Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so confirm the switched mode with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md — Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
19	
20	The `--detail` payload differs in two places between modes: `authentication` (`"connector"` vs `"manual"`), and the connector-binding fields `targetConnector` / `connectionId` / `folderKey` (connector mode only; `url` is then relative to the connector base, vs. an absolute URL in manual mode). Everything else (node add, dynamic values, branches, edges, debug) is shared.
21	
22	## Critical: Use `node configure`
23	
24	> **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, or connection resource files.** Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — it builds everything from a simple `--detail` JSON. Hand-written configurations miss the `essentialConfiguration` block and fail at runtime. `core.action.http.v2` is CLI-owned per [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) (same envelope rules as connector activities).
25	
26	## Registry validation
27	
28	```bash
29	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.http.v2 --output json
30	```
31	
32	Confirm in `Data.Node.handleConfiguration`: target port `input`, source ports `branch-{item.id}` (dynamic, `repeat: inputs.branches`) and `default`. Also confirm `Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling: true` — HTTP v2 participates in the implicit `error` port pattern shared by every action node (see [Action Node Structure](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md)). Model `serviceType` is `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest`.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Shared Reference (appendix)
37	
38	The mode walkthroughs link into the sections below for full rationale and extended examples. You do not need to read this section in order — jump directly from the walkthrough link that brought you here.
39	
40	### Add the node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
44	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance to `nodes[]`, registers the `variables.nodes` entries, and inserts a placeholder in `layout.nodes` — all in code, byte-for-byte from the registry (including `typeVersion`, which the CLI pulls from the manifest's `version` field; do not hardcode it). Save the returned node ID — both walkthroughs reuse it.
48	
49	The CLI initializes `inputs` from the manifest's `inputDefaults`:
50	
51	```json
52	"inputs": {
53	  "branches": [],
54	  "timeout": "PT15M",
55	  "retryCount": 0,
56	  "swaggerDefinition": null,
57	  "detail": {}
58	}
59	```
60	
61	`inputs.detail` is populated by the configure step (next). The inputs-level siblings — `branches`, `timeout`, `retryCount` — are set at `node add` time via `--input`:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
65	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
66	  --input '{
67	    "timeout": "PT30M",
68	    "retryCount": 3,
69	    "branches": [
70	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
71	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
72	    ]
73	  }' --output json
74	```
75	
76	- `timeout` — ISO 8601 duration (e.g. `PT15M`, `PT1H`, `P1D`). Default `PT15M`.
77	- `retryCount` — integer. Default `0`.
78	- `branches` — see [Conditional branches](#conditional-branches) below.
79	
80	> **Do not hand-author the `core.action.http.v2` definition, and do not `Edit` `inputs.*` after the fact.** Use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for branches/timeout/retryCount) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths.
81	
82	### Dynamic values in URL / headers / body / query
83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:
104	
105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```
113	
114	### Conditional branches
115	
116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).
117	
118	Each branch entry creates a `branch-{id}` source port. `$self` refers to the current HTTP node's output inside the condition.
119	
120	Set `branches` at `node add` time via `--input` (see [Add the node](#add-the-node)) — `branches` lives at `inputs.branches`, not `inputs.detail.branches`, and `node configure --detail` does not accept it.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
124	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
125	  --input '{
126	    "branches": [
127	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
128	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
129	    ]
130	  }' --output json
131	```
132	
133	> **Do not prefix `conditionExpression` with `=js:`** — HTTP branch conditions are auto-evaluated as JS (same rule as decision/switch expressions).
134	
135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set
142	
143	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`; do not use `uip maestro flow edge add` for this structural wiring. Examples:
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<errorHandlerId>",
168	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"
172	}
173	```
174	
175	When an HTTP node has an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly.
176	
177	```json
178	{
179	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",
180	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
181	  "sourcePort": "branch-hasItems",
182	  "targetNodeId": "<hasItemsDownstream>",
183	  "targetPort": "input"
184	}
185	```
186	
187	### Debug
188	
189	| Error | Cause | Fix |
190	| --- | --- | --- |
191	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
192	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
193	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
194	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
195	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |
196	| `ImplicitConnection` errors | Manual mode misconfigured | Verify `authentication: "manual"` and `url` is a full URL |
197	| Flow faults on 4xx/5xx response | No `error` edge wired from the HTTP node | Add an edge with `sourcePort: "error"` to an error-handler node. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — same mechanism applies to all action nodes |
198	| Edge `source-port output` rejected | Referencing the variable namespace as a port name | HTTP source ports are `default`, `error`, and `branch-{id}` — not `output`. The `output` name is only a variable namespace (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) |

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""NonCatalogHttpFallback: verify the agent uses a managed HTTP-request node for
3	a NON-catalog service that has no IS connector of its own (fixture: Spotify).
4	
5	Spotify is not a catalog connector — there is no ``uipath-spotify`` connector
6	key. The only way to reach it through Integration Service's managed auth is the
7	generic HTTP connector (``uipath-uipath-http``): a connection of that connector
8	type holds the Spotify base URL + OAuth, and the flow issues a connector-mode
9	HTTP request against it. The maestro-flow skill must therefore build a
10	``core.action.http.v2`` node bound to the ``uipath-uipath-http`` connection,
11	rather than searching for a native Spotify activity that does not exist.
12	
13	This is the non-catalog counterpart of the slack-http-fallback eval: there the
14	fallback proxies a catalog connector (``targetConnector`` = the Slack key);
15	here the connector key IS ``uipath-uipath-http`` because no catalog connector
16	backs the service.
17	
18	One check (subcommand-dispatched, like the outlook_trigger_inbox checker):
19	
20	  check_fallback   Structural — the profile fetch is a connector-mode
21	                   ``core.action.http.v2`` node whose connector key is
22	                   ``uipath-uipath-http`` with a bound connection, and it
23	                   targets Spotify's ``/me`` endpoint.
24	
25	``inputs.detail`` may be a dict (CLI-authored) or a ``=jsonString:``-prefixed
26	JSON envelope (hand-authored). Both shapes are normalised before inspection.
27	"""
28	
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	import glob
32	import json
33	import os
34	import sys
35	from typing import Any, NoReturn
36	
37	FLOW_GLOB = "**/SpotifyProfileTest*.flow"
38	# The generic HTTP connector — the only managed path to a service with no
39	# catalog connector of its own.
40	HTTP_CONNECTOR_KEY = "uipath-uipath-http"
41	# Spotify "Get Current User's Profile" endpoint.
42	ME_ENDPOINT = "/me"
43	_JSONSTRING_PREFIX = "=jsonString:"
44	
45	
46	def _fail(message: str) -> NoReturn:
47	    sys.exit(f"FAIL: {message}")
48	
49	
50	def _read_flow() -> dict[str, Any]:
51	    flows = sorted(glob.glob(FLOW_GLOB, recursive=True))
52	    if not flows:
53	        _fail(f"No flow file matching {FLOW_GLOB}")
54	    if len(flows) > 1:
55	        _fail(f"Multiple flows match {FLOW_GLOB}: {flows}")
56	    with open(flows[0], encoding="utf-8") as f:
57	        try:
58	            return json.load(f)
59	        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
60	            _fail(f"{flows[0]} is not valid JSON: {e}")
61	
62	
63	def _normalise_detail(raw: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
64	    if isinstance(raw, dict):
65	        return raw
66	    if isinstance(raw, str) and raw.startswith(_JSONSTRING_PREFIX):
67	        try:
68	            parsed = json.loads(raw[len(_JSONSTRING_PREFIX):])
69	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
70	            return {}
71	        return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else {}
72	    return {}
73	
74	
75	def _connection_bound(detail: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
76	    body = detail.get("bodyParameters") or {}
77	    candidates = [
78	        detail.get("connectionId"),
79	        detail.get("connectionResourceId"),
80	        body.get("connection") if isinstance(body, dict) else None,
81	    ]
82	    return any(
83	        isinstance(v, str) and v.strip() and v != "ImplicitConnection"
84	        for v in candidates
85	    )
86	
87	
88	def _is_http_connector_fallback(node: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
89	    """True when ``node`` is a connector-mode managed-HTTP node whose connector
90	    key is the generic ``uipath-uipath-http`` (the non-catalog fallback shape)."""
91	    node_type = str(node.get("type") or "").lower()
92	    if "core.action.http" not in node_type:
93	        return False
94	    detail = _normalise_detail((node.get("inputs") or {}).get("detail"))
95	    body = detail.get("bodyParameters") or {}
96	    auth = str(body.get("authentication") or "").lower() if isinstance(body, dict) else ""
97	    connector = str(detail.get("connector") or "").lower()
98	    target = (
99	        str(body.get("targetConnector") or body.get("connectorKey") or "").lower()
100	        if isinstance(body, dict)
101	        else ""
102	    )
103	    uses_http_connector = HTTP_CONNECTOR_KEY in (connector, target)
104	    return auth == "connector" and uses_http_connector and _connection_bound(detail)
105	
106	
107	def _targets_me_endpoint(node: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
108	    """True when the node's path/url is Spotify's ``/me`` endpoint. Matches the
109	    explicit field value (not a blob substring) so '/me' cannot spuriously match
110	    inside an unrelated path like '/members'."""
111	    detail = _normalise_detail((node.get("inputs") or {}).get("detail"))
112	    body = detail.get("bodyParameters") or {}
113	    if not isinstance(body, dict):
114	        return False
115	    for key in ("path", "url"):
116	        value = body.get(key)
117	        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip().rstrip("/").lower().endswith("/me"):
118	            return True
119	    return False
120	
121	
122	# ── subcommand: check_fallback ──────────────────────────────────────────────
123	def check_fallback() -> None:
124	    flow = _read_flow()
125	    if "nodes" not in flow or "edges" not in flow:
126	        _fail("Flow missing 'nodes' or 'edges'")
127	    nodes = flow["nodes"]
128	    print(f"OK: {len(nodes)} nodes, {len(flow['edges'])} edges")
129	
130	    fallback_nodes = [n for n in nodes if _is_http_connector_fallback(n)]
131	    if not fallback_nodes:
132	        types = sorted({str(n.get("type") or "") for n in nodes})
133	        _fail(
134	            "No managed HTTP-request node using the generic "
135	            f"{HTTP_CONNECTOR_KEY!r} connector found. Spotify is not a catalog "
136	            "connector, so the flow must issue a connector-mode "
137	            "core.action.http.v2 request bound to the uipath-uipath-http "
138	            f"connection. Node types seen: {types}"
139	        )
140	    print(
141	        f"OK: {len(fallback_nodes)} managed-HTTP node(s) bound to "
142	        f"{HTTP_CONNECTOR_KEY!r} with a connection present"
143	    )
144	
145	    if not any(_targets_me_endpoint(n) for n in fallback_nodes):
146	        _fail(
147	            f"No {HTTP_CONNECTOR_KEY!r} node targets the {ME_ENDPOINT!r} endpoint "
148	            "(expected the Spotify '/me' path, which returns the current user's "
149	            "profile)."
150	        )
151	    print(f"OK: fallback node targets Spotify's '{ME_ENDPOINT}' endpoint")
152	    print("OK: all Spotify HTTP-fallback structural checks passed")
153	
154	
155	DISPATCH = {
156	    "check_fallback": check_fallback,
157	}
158	
159	
160	def main() -> None:
161	    if len(sys.argv) < 2 or sys.argv[1] not in DISPATCH:
162	        _fail(f"usage: {os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])} {{{'|'.join(DISPATCH)}}}")
163	    DISPATCH[sys.argv[1]]()
164	
165	
166	if __name__ == "__main__":
167	    main()

1	# Managed HTTP Request - Concept + `http-request` Authoring Helper
2	
3	This doc covers two things every agent authoring a Managed HTTP Request needs to know:
4	1. What Managed HTTP Request is, and the two modes it runs in.
5	2. How to use the `http-request` CLI command to fill in the values Managed HTTP Request needs.
6	
7	Consumers: Maestro Flow, Maestro BPMN, API Workflows, Case Management, etc. Each consumer surfaces Managed HTTP Request differently (as a node, an activity, a tool call, …) and uses its own type identifier and configuration schema - the concept and the rules below are the same. For the exact node/activity type identifier and how to configure it, see your consumer's own authoring docs.
8	
9	## What is Managed HTTP Request?
10	
11	A built-in way to make an HTTP call from a UiPath automation. Runs in two modes - **connector mode** and **manual mode**:
12	
13	| Mode | When | `url` | Auth |
14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| **Connector** | Connector exists for the vendor but the specific operation is not curated | **Relative** to the connection's vendor base URL | Applied automatically from the bound connection |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, or public API with no auth needed | **Full URL** | You supply all headers, including auth |
17	
18	## Connector-Mode Rules
19	
20	- **Connector mode only works if the connector supports HTTP request activity** — verify by running `uip is connectors get "<connector-key>"` and checking the `HasHttpRequest` flag.
21	- `url` must be **relative**. Wrong: `"url": "https://example.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue"`. Right: `"url": "/issue"`.
22	- The connection's base URL is prepended automatically.
23	- The auth header is applied automatically - do not set `Authorization`.
24	- **`application/json` only - request and response.** No other content type is supported. File upload/download operations are the most common violation (`multipart/form-data`, `application/octet-stream`, binary/stream responses) - check the operation's request and response content types before authoring. If non-JSON, connector mode cannot call it - use a curated connector activity; if none exists, surface to the user.
25	- Get the exact vendor base URL for a connection via (so you can compose the relative `url` correctly):
26	
27	```bash
28	uip is connections base-url "<connection-id>" --output json
29	# → { "Data": { "BaseUrl": "https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<site>/rest/api/2" } }
30	```
31	
32	## Manual-Mode Rules
33	
34	- `url` is the **fully qualified URL**.
35	- No connection is bound - you supply everything needed to make the call: URL, headers (including auth if needed), query params, and body.
36	
37	## Step 0: Ground Against the Vendor's API Docs (registry) — connector mode only
38	
39	> **Connector mode only.** This grounding step applies when `authentication: "connector"` (a connector exists and the `url` is **relative** to its vendor base URL). Manual mode targets an arbitrary REST API with a full URL and has no connector to look up — skip this step for manual mode.
40	
41	**Before composing any `url` / `query` / `body`, ground the endpoint against the vendor's documentation.** Skipping this is the most common cause of a wrong-but-plausible endpoint that still "completes" at runtime (many vendors return HTTP 200 with an error body for an unknown path — e.g. Slack `{"ok":false,"error":"unknown_method"}` — so a bad path does not fault).
42	
43	1. Look the target connector up in [`vendor-docs-registry.json`](vendor-docs-registry.json) (same directory). Match by `connectorKey`.
44	2. **If listed:** read its `docsUrl` (authoritative API reference) and `notes` (vendor-specific conventions: endpoint shape, custom-field keys, query quirks). Honor the `notes` verbatim, then confirm the exact path with the `http-request` probe below (the live call is the final authority — the registry only grounds the baseline).
45	3. **If NOT listed:** this registry-grounding step does not apply. Proceed with the normal authoring flow — resolve the endpoint and any missing values via the `http-request` probe below, as you would otherwise.
46	
47	> **Pass endpoint paths verbatim — do NOT "REST-ify" them.** Many vendor APIs name operations with **literal dots**, where the whole dotted token is a single path segment: Slack`chat.postMessage`, `conversations.replies`. The dot is **not** a namespace separator — never rewrite `chat.postMessage` as `/chat/postMessage`. Copy the method exactly as the docs/registry show it (`"url": "/chat.postMessage"`).
48	
49	## Authoring Helper: `http-request` command
50	
51	Authoring a Managed HTTP Request payload requires concrete vendor values - IDs, field names, endpoint paths. Use `http-request` command to call any vendor API directly through the connection - same auth, same base URL the Managed HTTP Request will use at runtime.
52	
53	### When the Agent Needs `http-request` command
54	
55	Use `http-request` command to resolve any of the following before authoring the Managed HTTP Request payload:
56	
57	- **Identifier lookups.** Resolve a human-friendly name to the vendor's internal ID. Examples: project key from a project name, channel ID from a channel name, user ID from email/name, custom-field IDs.
58	- **Required and optional fields** the vendor expects in the request body
59	- **Endpoint paths, query params, pagination tokens** before committing to a payload
60	- **Vendor error responses** for unsupported parameters or permissions

60	- **Vendor error responses** for unsupported parameters or permissions
61	
62	### Command
63	
64	```bash
65	uip is resources run create "<connector-key>" http-request \
66	  --connection-id "<id>" \
67	  --body '{"method":"<method>","url":"<relative-path>"}' --output json
68	```
69	
70	| `body` field | Required | Notes |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| `method` | Yes | Uppercase HTTP verb |
73	| `url` | Yes | **Relative** to the connection's vendor base URL (same convention as Managed HTTP Request connector mode) |
74	| `headers` | No | Extra headers. Do NOT set `Authorization`. |
75	| `body` | For POST/PUT/PATCH | **Stringified** JSON. Only `application/json` is supported today — no other content type. |
76	
77	`http-request` command uses the same connection that Managed HTTP Request will use at runtime, so auth + base URL are applied automatically - same convention as Managed HTTP Request itself.
78	
79	### Read-Only During Authoring
80	
81	When using the `http-request` command, use `GET` method only, as `POST` / `PATCH` / `PUT` / `DELETE` mutate vendor state, often irreversibly.
82	
83	Exception: the user asks you to actually run the operation now, not just author it.
84	
85	## Worked Example: Jira Create Issue
86	
87	User wants to create a Jira issue. Before composing the Managed HTTP Request payload, the agent needs the project key, issue type ID, and required custom fields. All resolved via `http-request` command GETs.
88	
89	```bash
90	# 1. Resolve project key (user said "Engineering project").
91	uip is resources run create uipath-atlassian-jira http-request \
92	  --connection-id "<id>" \
93	  --body '{"method":"GET","url":"/project/search?query=Engineering"}' --output json
94	# → key "ENG"
95	
96	# 2. For project ENG, get available issue types + required custom fields.
97	uip is resources run create uipath-atlassian-jira http-request \
98	  --connection-id "<id>" \
99	  --body '{"method":"GET","url":"/issue/createmeta?projectKeys=ENG&expand=projects.issuetypes.fields"}' \
100	  --output json
101	# → match "Task" → id "10001"; required custom field: customfield_10010 (Story Points)
102	```
103	
104	3. (Optional) Confirm resolved values with the user.
105	
106	4. Compose the Managed HTTP Request payload. The actual configuration command and schema are consumer-specific — the request body Managed HTTP Request will send to Jira at runtime looks like:
107	
108	```json
109	{
110	  "method": "POST",
111	  "url": "/issue",
112	  "body": {
113	    "fields": {
114	      "project": { "key": "ENG" },
115	      "issuetype": { "id": "10001" },
116	      "summary": "Fix coder evals",
117	      "customfield_10010": 3
118	    }
119	  }
